subject: Anthropology
title: Organ Transplantation
description: A fast breakdown of Organ Transplantation for builders.

hook.text: You carry a stranger's heart in your chest. Whose person are you now? Organ transplants raise deep cultural questions.

buildup.text: Organ transplants challenge cultural ideas about personhood, death, the body, and the boundaries between self and other.

discovery.text: In many cultures, body parts carry identity. Recipients report feeling changed — sensing the donor's presence within.

twist.text: The global organ trade exploits the poor. Wealthy patients buy organs from desperate sellers in an unequal market.

climax.text: Organ transplants expose how medicine, markets, and meaning collide. The body becomes both gift and commodity.

punchline.text: A transplanted organ carries more than biology.

quiz.question: What cultural issue does organ transplantation raise?
options: Questions about personhood, identity, and the body as commodity

details.summary: Organ transplantation raises profound anthropological questions about body ownership, commodification, and the boundary between life and death. Global organ trafficking, cultural attitudes toward bodily integrity, and brain death definitions vary across societies.
details.whyItMatters: Organ transplantation reveals how cultural values about the body clash with biomedical technology. Questions about who donates to whom, at what price, and under what consent expose deep inequalities in global health systems.
takeaways: Organ transplantation raises issues of body ownership and commodification
Cultural attitudes toward bodily integrity affect donation rates
Global organ trade exposes deep inequalities in healthcare access

faq.question: Why do organ donation rates vary across cultures?
faq.answer: Religious beliefs about bodily resurrection, cultural taboos about bodily integrity, distrust of medical institutions, and different definitions of death all affect donation rates. Opt-out systems (presumed consent) produce higher donation rates than opt-in systems regardless of culture.

faq.question: What are the ethical issues with global organ trafficking?
faq.answer: Organs flow from poor to rich bodies — poor people in developing countries sell kidneys to wealthy patients from developed nations. This commodification of body parts raises profound ethical concerns about consent, exploitation, and whether economic desperation constitutes voluntary choice.
